title: How Sky GM Jeff Pagliocca set up WNBA rivals for success and left Chicago reeling - CBS Sports
description: The Chicago Sky were the only team watching the 2027 WNBA Draft Lottery on Sunday that was hoping for bad luck. The Sky went 16-28 last
body:
The Chicago Sky were the only team watching the 2027 WNBA Draft Lottery on Sunday that was hoping for bad luck. The Sky went 16-28 last season and haven't made the playoffs since 2023, but owe the Washington Mystics a 2027 first-round pick swap to complete a 2025 trade. The Mystics made the playoffs last season, so the pick was gone no matter what, but the higher it landed in the lottery, the worse the trade would look for the Sky. In the end, it came up at No. 3, right where it was projected based on the odds. Washington, which already has one of the brightest futures in the league, is now guaranteed to add one of JuJu Watkins, Hannah Hidalgo or Madison Booker. Chicago, which has one of the bleakest futures, will get Washington's No. 11 pick. So it has gone for the Sky since general manager Jeff Pagliocca's arrival. Since he was hired on Halloween in 2023, he has wheeled and dealed to little success for Chicago, while simultaneously setting up three other teams -- the Atlanta Dream, Washington Mystics and Minnesota Lynx -- with young franchise players. Angel Reese, Sonia Citron and Olivia Miles have all either been drafted by the Sky or with picks the Sky originally owned since Pagliocca took charge; none of them play in Chicago. Now, it looks like the Mystics will add one of Hidalgo or Booker, and that's not even the end of the misery, because Washington also owns the Sky's 2028 first-round pick outright. 
Here's a list of notable players and picks that have been traded away during Pagliocca's three-year tenure:Kahleah CopperJulie AllemandRebekah GardnerMarina MabreyDana EvansSonia Citron (No. 3 pick in 2025)Angel ReeseAriel AtkinsOlivia Miles (No. 2 pick in 2026)Frieda Bühner (No. 17 pick in 2026)No. 3 pick in 20272028 first-round pickOf course, some of these players asked out due to issues that pre-dated Pagliocca, but an absurd amount of talent has left Chicago (or never arrived) over the last three years.Following Sunday's draft lottery, let's take a look back at Pagliocca's first three years in Chicago to see how things have gone so wrong for the Sky, but so right for the teams that have traded with them.2024Trades Kahleah Copper to PhoenixPagliocca's first big move was trading 2021 Finals MVP Kahleah Copper and the rights to Morgan Bertsch to the Mercury for Brianna Turner, Michaela Onyenwere, the No. 3 pick in the 2024 WNBA Draft, Phoenix's 2026 first-round pick and some second-round picks. Copper would go on to help the Mercury reach the Finals in 2025. However, Copper wanted to leave Chicago and Pagliocca got a great return. This deal was a positive start to his tenure. 
Trades Julie Allemand to Los AngelesA few weeks after moving Copper, Pagliocca traded veteran point guard Julie Allemand to the Sparks for the No. 8 pick in the 2024 draft and the rights to Li Yueru. Allemand had only played two seasons in the WNBA to that point, had sat out in 2023 and ended up sitting out in 2024 as well. Again, another nice deal to acquire a top-10 pick. Trades Rebekah Gardner to New YorkA month later, Pagliocca traded Rebekah Gardner to the New York Liberty in exchange for two second-round picks. Gardner had missed most of the 2023 season with a broken foot and has never been the same player she was pre-injury. Another solid move. Trades for No. 7 pickJust before the 2024 WNBA Draft, Pagliocca acquired the No. 7 pick and Sika Koné from the Minnesota Lynx in exchange for the No. 8 pick, the rights to Nikolina Milić, a 2026 first-round pick swap and a second-round pick. This is where the wheels started to fall off. Giving up a future first-round swap at the beginning of a rebuild was unnecessarily risky and would come back to haunt them. 
Drafts Kamilla Cardoso and Angel ReeseIn the 2024 WNBA Draft, Pagliocca selected Kamilla Cardoso (No. 3) and Angel Reese (No. 7). Immediately, there were major questions about drafting two bigs who could not space the floor just as the league was moving toward a more perimeter-oriented game. The Sky's interest in Reese was an open secret ahead of the draft, which made their decision to draft Cardoso at No. 3 even more confusing. In a vacuum, Cardoso was a very reasonable pick at No. 3, but if they were confident in getting Reese at No. 7, why not draft Rickea Jackson -- the best wing in the class -- at No. 3? (Ironically, Jackson is now on the team.)Pagliocca's belief in Reese was well-founded, and she became the steal of that draft. Cardoso, on the other hand, has never developed the way anyone hoped. While she's put up solid numbers throughout her career, she has not impacted winning. Let's take a look at the on/off data from Cardoso and Reese's two seasons together in Chicago. 
LineupMinutesNet RatingCardoso and Reese1,168-5.1Reese only884-3.7Cardoso only803-19.4Trades Marina Mabrey to ConnecticutAhead of the 2024 trade deadline, Pagliocca tarded Marina Mabrey and a second-round pick to the Connecticut Sun in exchange for Rachel Banham, Moriah Jefferson, the Sun's 2025 first-round pick and a 2026 first-round pick swap. Mabrey requested a trade, and getting a first-round pick and a pick swap for someone who, to that point, had never made an All-Star appearance, was a nice bit of business, especially given the lack of leverage. 2025Trades with Connecticut for Rebecca Allen Pagliocca's first move of the 2025 offseason was to trade Lindsay Allen and Milić to the Sun for Rebecca Allen. This was a smart deal that just didn't pan out. Lindsay Allen and Milić have done nothing since then, and it wasn't Pagliocca's fault that Rebecca Allen had one of the worst 3-point shooting seasons of her career in 2025. Trades Dana Evans to Las VegasDana Evans, who was part of the 2021 championship team, was a restricted free agent in 2025 and made it clear she wanted a bigger role. In a sign-and-trade deal, Pagliocca traded Evans to the Aces for two second-round picks in the 2025 draft, which later became Maddy Westbeld and Aicha Coulibaly. Westbeld is no longer with the Sky, but Coulibaly had some promising moments as a rookie in 2026. Getting two swings in the draft for a player who wanted to leave in free agency was decent business. Trades No. 3 pick to WashingtonThe Sky went 13-27 in 2024 and received the No. 3 overall pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft, which put them in a tricky spot. At the time, Paige Bueckers and Olivia Miles (who ended up staying in school) were expected to go 1-2 in that draft, which meant the Sky were going to have to reach to get the guard they really needed at No. 3, take a big, even though they had just drafted Cardoso and Reese, or trade the pick. Pagliocca chose the latter and decided to make a win-now move. In late February, he sent the No. 3 pick, a 2027 first-round pick swap and a 2027 second-round pick to the Mystics in exchange for Ariel Atkins. Atkins was a two-time All-Star and five-time All-Defensive honoree who had won a title with the Mystics in 2019 and gold medals with Team USA at the 2020 Olympics and 2022 World Cup. While everyone expected that Atkins would make the Sky better, the deal was widely criticized at the time as a short-sighted overpay -- especially when the Sky were so far away from making any serious noise in the playoffs and Atkins was set to be an unrestricted free agent in 2026. The Mystics ended up taking Sonia Citron at No. 3, who exceeded all expectations and is now one of the best young players in the league. She's been an All-Star in each of her first two seasons, won a gold medal with Team USA at the 2026 World Cup and was named to the All-Defensive Team last season. Atkins was solid in what wound up being her lone season in Chicago: 13.1 points, 3.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.6 steals, but she did not move the needle. In fact, the Sky were actually worse in 2025 than they were in 2024. They finished in a tie for last place at 10-34, which at the time set the single-season losses record. Giving up Citron for one season of Atkins would have been a disaster on its own, but now it's Citron and the No. 3 pick in the 2027 draft. Just a total disaster. This will go down as one of the worst deals in WNBA history. Trades for No. 11 pickJust before the 2025 WNBA Draft, Pagliocca swung a deal with the Lynx to acquire the No. 11 pick in exchange for extinguishing the 2026 first-round pick swap between the two teams. As a result, the Lynx got the Sky's 2026 first-round pick outright. 
The Lynx were coming off a Finals appearance and were one of the favorites heading into the 2025 season, while the Sky were coming off a 10-win campaign. The pick swap was almost certainly going to convey in 2026 (and it did), so Pagliocca took the No. 11 pick in 2025 rather than what would have been the No. 15 pick in 2026. Decent value bet that ultimately didn't work out. Drafts Ajša Sivka and Hailey Van LithThe Sky had the Nos. 10 and 11 picks in the 2025 WNBA Draft via Connecticut and Minnesota. At No. 10, Pagliocca selected Ajša Sivka and at No. 11 he took Hailey Van Lith. Sivka stayed in Europe in 2025 and eventually chose to go the college route. She is now a freshman at Kentucky, where she's off to a stellar start. The Sky retain her rights, and this may wind up being a great pick in the long run. Van Lith barely played during her rookie season and was waived during training camp in 2026. 
Giving up Citron, then getting nothing (at least so far) from your other two first-round picks in that class was a major setback for the Sky. The Van Lith pick, in particular, was a major error, especially after trading with the Lynx to cancel the 2026 swap rights and take the No. 11 pick. 2026Buys protection from the double expansion draftAhead of the 2026 season, the league held a double expansion draft for the Portland Fire and Toronto Tempo. The current teams were allowed to protect five players from selection. Pagliocca opted to ensure that neither the Fire nor the Tempo selected any Sky players by buying protection. 
He traded the No. 17 overall pick to the Fire for the No. 21 overall pick and a promise not to select any Sky players. He also traded the No. 26 overall pick to the Tempo for a promise not to select any Sky players. The Fire selected Frieda Bühner at No. 17, who had a promising rookie season. The Sky took Latasha Lattimore at No. 21; she did not make their roster. The Tempo took Shaffron Shiels at No. 26; she remained overseas last season. Were these deals the end of the world? No, but they were further examples of poor asset management. The 2025 Sky didn't have more than five players worth protecting, and dropping out of the top-20 and giving up another second-round pick in the process cost them a chance at Bühner, Charlisse Leger-Walker and Cassandre Prosper, all of whom were contributing players as rookies last season. Trades Angel Reese to AtlantaThe relationship between Reese and the Sky deteriorated quickly toward the end of the 2025 season. Reese gave a controversial interview to the Chicago Tribune in which she criticized the front office, coaching staff and her teammates, and insinuated that she would not re-sign after her rookie contract was up if the team's fortunes didn't change. 
Reese later apologized to her teammates and the organization, both publicly and privately, and the team suspended her for the first half of a game against the Aces -- a strange decision that only inflamed the situation. While Reese said in Dec. 2025 that she planned to return to the Sky, a split always seemed possible. Sure enough, Pagliocca traded her to the Atlanta Dream for first-round picks in 2027 and 2028 as soon as the league was open for business last offseason. While ESPN reported that Reese did not demand a trade, she did work with the organization on trade talks to find her a new team. The trade was immediately regarded as a disaster for the Sky that only got worse as the season went along. Reese won Defensive Player of the Year, made the All-WNBA Second Team and All-Defensive First Team, and led the Dream to the Finals, while the Sky went 16-28 and missed the playoffs again. Meanwhile, the Sky had to give up the No. 2 overall pick in the draft to the Lynx, which closed the book on the trade that brought Reese to Chicago in the first place. The Lynx drafted Miles, who was named the unanimous Rookie of the Year. Trades 2028 first to Washington
Amid a frenzy of moves last offseason, Pagliocca traded the Sky's 2028 first-round pick to the Mystics for Jacy Sheldon. While it was one thing to have interest in the former No. 5 overall pick as a reclamation project, giving up a 2028 first-round pick for her was baffling in the moment and could get exponentially worse. Sheldon averaged 6.4 points and 1.8 assists, and shot a career-worst 30% from 3-point range as the Sky finished 10 games out of the playoffs. Her poor play was part of the reason the Sky wound up in the lottery again and had to give the Mystics the No. 3 pick. Which, in turn, will make it more likely that the Sky miss the playoffs again next season and have to give the Mystics another lottery pick in 2028. Pagliocca can argue that he was put in a bad spot or had some bad luck on some of his previous trades. Not so on this one. This trade never made sense, and could result in the Sky giving up lottery picks in four consecutive drafts. It's particularly confusing how Pagliocca was swindled by the Mystics again before the 2025 deal was even complete. Trades Atkins to Los AngelesSpeaking of the 2025 deal with the Mystics, Pagliocca's third trade last offseason was flipping Atkins to the Sparks for Rickea Jackson -- the No. 4 pick in the 2024 draft, whom he should have selected at the time at No. 3 instead of Cardoso. Pagliocca rightfully received praise for finding a way to flip Atkins for a young player with All-Star potential and salvaging some value from the 2025 Mystics trade. Jackson was excellent to start last season, and helped the Sky get off to a 3-1 start before tearing her ACL. She missed the remainder of 2026, and it's unclear when she'll be available in 2027. Jackson's injury was a short- and long-term disaster. Her absence played a big role in the Sky missing the playoffs, which meant giving up the No. 3 pick. And it's unclear when she'll be back on the court again, or if she'll get back to her pre-injury level. If she's not available and at her best for most of the 2027 season, there's a good chance the Sky have to give up another lottery pick to the Mystics in 2028. Drafts Gabriela Jaquez ahead of Kiki RiceWhile the Sky had to give up the No. 2 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft to the Lynx, they did still have a lottery selection via the Sun, which checked in at No. 5. In a major shock, Pagliocca selected Gabriela Jaquez ahead of former UCLA teammate Kiki Rice and Flau'jae Johnson. Rice was always a much better pro prospect than Jaquez, and the Sky needed a point guard for the future. While Jaquez got off to a great start as a rookie, she soon faded and was out of the rotation for a stretch late in the season. There's still a good chance she's a solid player, but Rice, who made the All-Rookie Team despite playing just 28 games due to a severe ankle sprain, looks like a future All-Star. What's next?Turnarounds are always possible in the WNBA, but the future is murky for the Sky.The collection of players that have been traded away from the Sky in the past three years have combined for seven All-Star appearances, two All-WNBA appearances, two All-Defensive appearances, one Defensive Player of the Year and one Rookie of the Year award, three Finals appearances and one championship since leaving Chicago. Those accolades are going to keep rising because Reese, Miles and Citron, in particular, are three of the best young players in the league. And if the No. 3 pick in 2027 and the 2028 first-round pick are even close to that trio's level, the Sky's misery will only get worse.

title: Jake Bauers contract: Red Sox sign slugging first baseman to four-year, $58 million deal - CBS Sports
description: Bauers broke out this past season, slugging 26 home runs that more than doubled his previous career high
body:
Bauers broke out this past season, slugging 26 home runs that more than doubled his previous career high

    2:18 pm ET

        The Boston Red Sox have made the offseason's first major free agent signing. The Red Sox and first baseman Jake Bauers have agreed to a four-year contract worth a reported $58 million, the team announced on Tuesday.Bauers, 31, broke out with the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers this past season, authoring a .266/.389/.484 batting line with 26 home runs that more than doubled his previous career high (12). He was named the NLCS MVP during Milwaukee's title run thanks to a 4 for 14 (.286) effort. Bauers drove in seven runs in the four-game sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers.
The Red Sox desperately needed a power bat and certainly added one with Bauers. Their 163 home runs this past season were the fifth fewest in baseball and three players -- Wilyer Abreu, Willson Contreras and Jarren Duran -- accounted for 71 of those 163 home runs. Boston's lineup figures to look something like this with Bauers now added:LF Roman Anthony, LHBC Adley Rutschman, SHBDH Jake Bauers, LHB1B Willson Contreras, RHBRF Wilyer Abreu, LHB2B Curtis Mead, RHBCF Ceddanne Rafaela, RHB3B Caleb Durbin, RHBSS Trevor Story, RHBThat leaves Duran without a full-time position and makes a trade or even a non-tender more likely. Franklin Arias, one of the very best prospects in the minors, could debut early next season and wrestle the shortstop job away from Story. POBO Craig Breslow recently said Story is not locked in as the team's starting shortstop.
We ranked Bauers as the 12th-best free agent available this offseason, and the seventh-best position player free agent. Here's our write-up:Rake Bauers (finally) lived up to the nickname this year and carried it over into the postseason, particularly during the NLCS. Long an exit velocity and hard-hit rate darling, Bauers fully tapped into his power in 2026 thanks to a more open stance and moving back in the box and further off the plate. That allowed him to see the ball better and get his bat into the hitting position on time more consistently. I'm not 100% sold on those adjustments solving his career-long issues with lefties, though at least there is a tangible reason to believe in his great left-on-left performance this season. Bauers can be an adventure in the field (he has played outfield in the past) and he just turned 31. A few teams will look for the next Jake Bauers rather than pay the actual Jake Bauers.The Brewers tendered Bauers the $23.15 million qualifying offer and will receive a 2027 compensation draft pick after the first round because the contract exceeds $50 million. Because they paid the competitive balance tax, the Red Sox will forfeit their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in bonus pool money for the 2027 international signing period, to sign Bauers.Milwaukee could turn to Tyler Black and Andrew Vaughn at first base next season. Andrew Fischer, the No. 20 overall pick in the 2025 draft, slugged 48 home runs in the minors this summer and reached Double-A. He is the long-term solution at first base but is likely a year away from the big leagues. The Brewers could bring in a stopgap first baseman if they're not sold on Black.
The Red Sox went 87-75 this past season and were the second wild card team. They were swept by the rival New York Yankees in the Wild Card Series and scored only two runs in the two games.

title: Josh Hokit calls for rematch with Ciryl Gane after disputed loss at UFC 334 - CBS Sports
description: Gane poked Hokit in the eye early in round 1 of their heavyweight championship fight
body:
Gane poked Hokit in the eye early in round 1 of their heavyweight championship fight
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:01 pm ET

        Josh Hokit came up just short of capturing the UFC heavyweight championship with a spirited effort against champion Ciryl Gane at UFC 334 this past Saturday. Now, Hokit is calling for a rematch with Gane and using an early Gane eye poke as a primary reason for another shot at gold.Early in the first round of their fight at Madison Square Garden in New York, Gane reached toward Hokit's face and his finger clearly went into Hokit's eye. Hokit reacted to the foul, but referee Marc Goddard did not see it, and thus, Gane was not punished.Hokit would go on to lose a narrow unanimous decision that many felt he had edged out through the application of relentless pressure that forced Gane out of his comfort zone as a tactical striker. Still, the judges favored Gane's striking edge over Hokit's pressure, and Hokit was not able to capture heavyweight gold just over one year after making his Octagon debut.On Tuesday, Hokit responded to a video of former middleweight champion Robert Whittaker breaking down the fight by calling for an immediate rematch, addressing his Tweets to UFC and promotion CEO Dana White.

Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!"He completely poked my eye out 40 [seconds] into the fight," Hokit wrote. "I complained and got no help. Blinded, I had every excuse to walk away and blow up the entire event. But I didn't quit on you, and I didn't quit on the fans. I care about this sport way too much to ever take the easy way out. I'm not a bitch. Most people know I won that night. Thats why I am making the case that we should run it back."Hokit also cited how he believes the scoring criteria of the Unified Rules of Mixed Martial Arts should have resulted in the decision going in his favor.

        
            
                UFC 334 fight fallout: Best options for Ciryl Gane, Josh Hokit, Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes after Saturday
                
                    Shakiel Mahjouri                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
"They want to talk about stats?" Hokit continued. "Let's talk about the Unified Rules. Judges score on effective striking and impact, not patting someone with light, non damaging touches. Ciryl sprinted away from me for 3 straight rounds while I relentlessly stalked him down and landed the heavier shots. Volume that doesn't hurt nobody isn't winning a fight. Effective Aggressivenes & Ring Generalship belonged to me for the first 3. That's why my coaches thought I was winning going into the 5th and his coach told him he needed a knckout...Lets not forget that."Hokit would go on to point out that, had Gane been deducted a point for the eye poke in the first round, he would have at least earned a draw.Had the referee seen the foul, it's unclear if it would have resulted in an immediate point deduction, but Gane has likely lost the benefit of the doubt when it comes to bending the rules.
Gane has a history of landing eye pokes or illegal blows in his fight, most infamously delivering a poke to both of Tom Aspinall's eyes so bad in their UFC 321 bout that then-champion Aspinall would end up vacating the title, leaving Gane to be elevated to undisputed champion after winning the interim title in Aspinall's absence.Hokit closed by pointing to the lack of fresh challengers for Gane, claiming to be the most interesting rematch available for the champion, who has fought nearly every other contender of note in the division."Look at the division," Hokit wrote. "Almost any fight you make with Ciryl right now is a recycled rematch anyway, whether it's Volkov or Alex. But our war was the best by a mile, and the fans deserve a definitive answer without a finger in my eye that had me seeing triple, 40 seconds into the fight. I earned this. Don't punish me because I am not a bitch. Let's make it right."

        The NFL is flexing its scheduling freedom, moving the Week 12 Las Vegas Raiders at Cleveland Browns matchup from 1 p.m. ET to "Sunday Night Football." The New England Patriots were originally scheduled to play the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium in prime time that week, but that matchup will now move to 4:05 p.m. ET. Tennessee Titans at Jacksonville Jaguars, which was originally scheduled for 4:05 p.m. ET that week moves to 1 p.m. ET.The Raiders-Browns matchup will feature Las Vegas's newest quarterback, Fernando Mendoza. The No. 1 overall pick took over after Vegas (4-6) sent Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings at the trade deadline last Tuesday, and Week 12 will mark the first prime-time matchup of his career. Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards in his first career start on Sunday, which came in a 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. As for the Browns, they moved to 6-4 last week following a remarkable comeback win over the Houston Texans. The 17-0 deficit Deshaun Watson and Co. overcame made it the second-largest comeback win at home in franchise history, while the Browns are now a perfect 4-0 in their home stadium for the first time since 1963. Cleveland currently holds the last wild-card spot in the AFC (No. 7 seed), behind the 6-3 Pittsburgh Steelers and 7-2 Denver Broncos.
The 5-5 Patriots are being flexed out of prime time following their disastrous 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich. The team reportedly fears that quarterback Drake Maye, who suffered a lower-leg injury early in the game, could be sidelined for an extended period of time. The injury could force last year's MVP runner-up to miss the remainder of the season. New England's Week 12 opponent, the Chargers, actually just tallied their first win of the season on Monday night, defeating Jacoby Brissett's Baltimore Ravens, 23-20.The NFL implemented this "flexible scheduling" rule in 2006. body:
Cam Ward's recent Fantasy surge and favorable matchup with Dallas make him a top streaming option as six teams hit their bye

    5:11 pm ET

        For some Tennessee Titans fans, the dream that Cam Ward would save the franchise may be fading. Ward is now 4-22 as a starter, is only averaging 190 passing yards per game in his second year, and has not seen his underlying stats improve in a meaningful way. But for Fantasy managers, the dream that Cam Ward may save your Week 11 is very much alive.It's worth saying that part of the reason we are talking about Cam Ward is the fact that Jordan Love, Matthew Stafford, Drake Maye, Drew Lock, Deshaun Watson, and Michael Penix are all on bye. It's also worth saying that Maye and Lock could be done for the year. Maye's ankle injury is serious and Sam Darnold could be back when the Seahawks return from bye. But let's not forget to give a little bit of credit to Ward's recent Fantasy success.In Week 9, Ward threw for 304 yards and two touchdowns against the Bengals. Yes, the same Bengals that just made Aaron Rodgers look miserable in Week 10. Ward followed that up with a gritty performance against the Jaguars, in which he scored 20 points without Carnell Tate. He's run for 80 yards in the past two games combined, which has certainly helped.In Week 11, things look even better. Once the lockout becomes official, the signings -- and all other transactions -- will cease, but the ones that happen before then will still count toward whenever baseball is allowed to resume. So we'd better document them all here, just like any other offseason, breaking down their impact for Fantasy Baseball.    That's what Scott White and Chris Towers intend to do over the next few weeks, at least, before everything goes quiet. The goal then would be to pick up where they left off when the hot stove heats up again in ... March? Hopefully not much later than that. description: Here are your hot stove rumors for Tuesday, Nov. 17
body:
Here are your hot stove rumors for Tuesday, Nov. 17
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:27 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The annual GM Meetings came and went last week with two significant transactions. The Braves signed reliever Evan Phillips (three years and $35 million) and the Red Sox signed slugger Jake Bauers (four years and $58 million). Bauers will give Boston some desperately needed home run power. Phillips will pair with Robert Suarez in the late innings for Atlanta.    Otherwise, we're still waiting on the winter's first true blockbuster, and the clock is ticking with a lockout expected upon the collective bargaining agreement's expiration at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Tuesday's hot stove happenings. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Rangers fielding calls about Gore
Teams are calling the Rangers about left-hander MacKenzie Gore, who is a year away from free agency, according to The Athletic. There is some reluctance to trade for players with only one year of control because games could be lost to a work stoppage next year, but pitching is so in-demand that at least some clubs are exploring a deal for Gore.Now 27, Gore is one of only six pitchers to make at least 30 starts in each of the last three years. His under-the-hood numbers (3.87 FIP and 4.19 expected ERA) were much better than his 4.58 actual ERA, plus he has long been considered to have untapped upside. Gore will give you innings, at minimum, and there's a chance his best days are ahead of him.

                            
    
                                                
                    
     Red Sox exploring trades for starters, Duran
The Red Sox are exploring the trade market for righties Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck, and Johan Oviedo, according to WEEI. They are also believed to be preparing to trade Jarren Duran, reports MassLive.com. Duran is a potential non-tender candidate if the Red Sox are unable to find a trade partner prior to Friday's deadline. The Mariners and Phillies are among the teams that are "poking around."Crawford, Houck, and Ovideo all missed significant time with injuries in 2026 (Crawford has not appeared in an MLB game since 2024) and are far down Boston's rotation depth chart. Duran has been pushed out of the everyday lineup by the recent Jake Bauers signing. Exploring trades for these four players in a seller's market is a sensible approach.
                            
    
                                                
                    
      Mets met with Skubal  
The Mets had an in-person meeting with top-ranked free agent Tarik Skubal on Monday, reports the New York Post. Owner Steve Cohen and president of baseball operations David Stearns were among those in attendance, according to SNY. Skubal and agent Scott Boras will meet with the Blue Jays, Dodgers, Padres, and potentially two other teams in the coming days.  
Skubal is expected to sign before the lockout and is therefore working on a tight schedule, much tighter than usual for top Boras clients. Nolan McLean and Christian Scott give the Mets two promising young arms to build around, but they need to improve the rotation around them, and Skubal would give the club a no-doubt ace to lead the pitching staff.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
      Cubs showing interest in Rogers  
The pitching-needy Cubs have shown interest in free agent lefty Trevor Rogers, reports The Athletic. Chicago needs multiple starters this offseason and has cast a wide net in their search. Justin Steele (UCL) and Ben Brown (neck), ostensibly the Cubs' No. 1 and 2 starters, are both recovering from surgeries, and Brown is expected to miss the start of 2027.    We ranked Rogers as the third-best free agent available this offseason because he is very good as is, and because he'll make analytical models hum with the quality of his arsenal and strike-throwing. Nine pitchers made at least nine starts for the Cubs in 2026 and only two -- Javier Assad and Edward Cabrera -- currently remain under contract/team control.  

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
      Orioles, Yankees interested in Arozarena  
The AL East rival Orioles and Yankees are among the teams with interest in free agent slugger Randy Arozarena, according to the Baltimore Banner and New York Post. The O's also have some interest in re-signing Luis Robert Jr. Other than Dylan Beavers and maybe Tyler O'Neill, Baltimore's outfield is wide open right now. They have DH at-bats available too.  It is likely the Yankees checked in on Arozarena out of due diligence more than serious interest. His righty bat would help their lefty-heavy lineup, though he would be a clunky roster fit as a corner outfielder who really needs to DH on a team that already has plenty of corner outfielders who really need to DH. If Arozarena's market is slow to develop, perhaps New York would pounce.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
      Rockies more willing to move Goodman?  
Teams around the league believe the Rockies are more open to trading All-Star catcher Hunter Goodman now than they were at the trade deadline, reports MLB Network. Colorado is said to have set a very high asking price for Goodman, who in 2026 became just the tenth primary catcher with a 40-homer season. He hit more homers on the road (25) than at Coors Field (16) too.  
Ryan Jeffers and Carson Kelly represent viable free agent alternatives to Goodman as right-handed offense-first catchers, though Goodman is several years younger than both and will have a lower salary the next three years through arbitration. Teams will likely feel more confident in Goodman holding his production for another few years than Jeffers and Kelly.

        Serbian standout Matija Lukic committed to Duke on Tuesday as one of the headliners for its 2027 class as coach Jon Scheyer continues to scour the globe for talent. Lukic made his pledge to the Blue Devils after visits this month to Duke, North Carolina, Boston College and UConn.The 6-foot-8, 200-pound forward is a four-star prospect per 247Sports and is the fourth commit for Duke's No. 4-ranked 2027 recruiting class. Lukic joins four-star commits Asa Montgomery, Kager Knueppel and Australia's Luke Paul with the Blue Devils.

247Sports director of scouting Adam Finkelstein, who watched Lukic up close earlier this month, describes the 17-year-old standout as a jumbo wing "with an overlap of perimeter size and well-rounded ball-skills" and crafty passer.
"He's a good ball-handler and passer who moves without the ball and can even initiate some possessions," Finkelstein writes in his advanced scouting report. "He doesn't necessarily have the first-step of a dynamic creator, but he pushes the ball up the floor with his head up, is a willing ball-mover with a high ceiling as a passer, and has some sneaky burst when he can rip-and-go immediately off the catch."He's a good, not necessarily, great shooter, who generates most of his power from his arms, leaning back into a high and compact release above his head. He has good rotation and deep range, but can have a harder ball at times, and is also much better when his feet are set than when on the move. Statistically, the sample sizes are limited, but still streaky. He was 42% from three in 7 games at the 2026 World Cup, but under 30% with his club team in both 2025 and 2026.
"Physically, he has great perimeter size but short arms, narrow shoulders, and high hips. He gets knocked around a little bit, but doesn't shy away from contact. He obviously needs to get stronger and should fill-out fine, but his high center of gravity could still be problematic in the lane and defensively."

        Breakthrough UFC star Tommy McMillen was reportedly hospitalized over the weekend after being found unresponsive in a nightclub bathroom.McMillen was rushed to the hospital on Sunday, police officers in Scottsdale, Arizona, told TMZ, after he was found unresponsive at CAKE Nightclub, a nightclub located in the city's Old Town district. According to the publication, responding officers removed McMillen from the bathroom and administered Narcan after discovering a white, powdery substance on the floor nearby. McMillen made an appearance on "The Joe Rogan Experience" on Tuesday where he discussed what happened."I had a few different substances on me and maybe mixed the wrong substances, or maybe had a bad batch of something. I guess my body gave out and I started to almost choke," McMillen said. "Stuff was coming out of my mouth, and I was almost choking on it. I was unresponsive. I don't remember any of this. I don't even remember getting to the club that night. They had to give me two Narcan [shots] or something like that, take me to the hospital and give me an IV. I think that happened around 11 p.m. at night or 12 a.m. I didn't wake up and come to until 5 a.m. the next day. I was out for six or seven hours." 
Narcan, also known as naloxone hydrochloride, is a medication designed to rapidly reverse a life-threatening opioid overdose. It is typically administered as a nasal spray or injected into a large muscle. McMillen was reportedly in stable condition and didn't appear to suffer any life-threatening complications."I try to be smart most of the time, but if I'm really drunk and already faded, my judgment starts to go down a little bit," he said. "At that point, I probably could've taken way more than I already took of something, and I wouldn't have even known. I probably would've swallowed a whole bag of something, just not even knowing, because I'm so faded."
McMillen has emerged as one of the MMA promotion's most popular young prospects. McMillen, a training partner of former UFC champion Sean O'Malley, earned his UFC contract on "Dana White's Contender Series." His brash personality and action-oriented style have won over parts of the fanbase, who affectionately refer to him as Tommy "Gun." Tim Welch, McMillen's head coach, posted that "Tommy is completely OK and training yesterday" on Nov. 12, once the news started circulating. McMillen credited his girlfriend for inspiring him to slow down, though he admitted that he's unsure about exactly how to adjust his habits in light of the recent scare.
"I have a girlfriend in my life, and she doesn't do drugs, and it's probably the best infuence in my life," McMillen said. "She doesn't do drugs or party like that, really. It's the first thing in my life in a long time that's made me want to make better decisions and be a better version of myself. Obviously, it didn't help much a week ago.""It's a wake up call, but I don't know if I'm going to stop partying cold turkey and f---ing become a f---ing, what do you guys want me to do?"

As federally regulated markets, they are both widely available throughout the United States, giving interested fans easier access to motor sports trading. Polymarket's offer is similar. Users who deposit $10 receive $25 in trading credits. What do motor sports odds mean?When it comes to motorsports and racing markets, odds are displayed and read similarly to how they are for most sports. Let's say a driver is priced at -150 to win the Monaco Grand Prix on June 7th, and the next best driver has +200 odds. That means the driver at -150 is a decent favorite to win, and you'd have to risk $150 to win $100. The second driver is a contender but is unlikely to win in the eyes of oddsmakers, but you'd win $200 after risking $100 if he does indeed pull off the upset.When you can bet on motor sports oddsThe racing schedule varies across NASCAR, F1 and IndyCar but there are usually weekly races with occasional breaks. NASCAR has multiple series, so there's usually at least one race across the series every weekend. F1 has a set calendar for the year with some breaks in between, but there are junior Formula racing series that might be going on in some of the gaps on the main circuit.Typically, the actual race will take place on a Sunday. There will be practice on either Thursday or Friday, with a qualifying event to set up the grid on either Friday or Saturday depending on the race schedule. Qualifying usually takes place the day before the race. Bettors can wager on qualifying outcomes as well, and those results will shift the race odds.Biggest races for motor sports bettingArguably, the biggest sporting event in the racing world is the Indianapolis 500, which is traditionally held on Memorial Day weekend. That's the premier IndyCar event.NASCAR has several big races, with the Daytona 500, a Crown Jewel event, regarded as the richest race on the circuit. The Coca-Cola 600 at Charlotte and the Brickyard 400 are also considered Crown Jewel events. Talladega Speedway is a widely known track thanks to the movie "Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby", but it is not a Crown Jewel event.Every F1 race has its unique twist. The tracks are different in each city, but Monaco is considered the biggest spectacle of the season. The race itself is somewhat mundane because there's little opportunity for drivers to pass each other. The British Grand Prix at Silverstone, the Italian Grand Prix at Monza and the Singapore Grand Prix are considered some marquee events on the F1 calendar. The Abu Dhabi Grand Prix is also a high-profile event as it is typically last on the calendar and could decide who wins the drivers championship and constructors championship. F1 has also added special events like Miami and Las Vegas.Types of bets and how motor sports betting works Like all sports betting markets, there are a variety of ways prospective bettors can wager on motor sports. Here's a look at some of them.Outright/To win oddsThis market is straightforward. Users are betting on which driver will win the event. There are also markets here for which team/constructor car will win the event, which will have multiple cars involved.Here are the odds to win the Las Vegas Grand Prix, taking place on November 21, 2026. Odds are courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook and are current as of November 17, 2026.Max Verstappen +135Andrea Kimi Antonelli +300Lando Norris +500George Russell +600Isack Hadjar +1800Placement/Top Finish oddsMotor sports betting offers users the ability to wager on drivers or teams having a certain placement or finishing within a certain range. For example, you can wager on drivers to place in the top 5 or top 10 of the event. You can do the same with teams/constructors.While it rarely occurs in racing, there's a possibility of multiple drivers tying for a position. In this case, there are  technically multiple winning bets. However, sportsbooks grade dead heats differently and the payouts can be different. If FanDuel declares a dead heat, half the stake is applied at the original odds and half the stake is lost. If there are more than two dead heats, the stakes are proportioned accordingly.Dual ForecastThis is where bettors can place a wager on which drivers will finish first and second. Both drivers must finish in the correct order for this wager to be paid out as a win. For example, you can wager on Max Verstappen and Lando Norris to finish first and second, respectively in a Dual Forecast market in F1 betting. However, if Verstappen finishes second and Norris finishes first, your bet will lose even though you did correctly pick the top two drivers for the race.Each Way BettingThis is not as common in motor sports but can be applied to racing betting. An each way bet basically places two wagers: a driver to win and to finish above another position. If the driver wins, both bets get paid out. The same applies for team bets in this market.Stage WinnerThis is prevalent in NASCAR and IndyCar, which has more laps than Formula One. You can bet on which driver or team will be in the lead after 25 laps, 50 laps, 100 laps and so on. These are the stages.Matchups/Head-to-HeadSportsbooks will put two drivers or two teams against each other, allowing bettors to choose which one will place higher. For teams, the bet is usually on the highest-placed driver for that particular team. This is one of the more popular F1 betting strategies. For example, if a market was being offered on F1 to see if Ferrari or Mercedes placed higher, the highest-placing Ferrari driver determines the result, even if both Mercedes drivers finish ahead of the second Ferrari driver. This means that bettors must consider both driver and car in situations like this.Group WinnerThis is offered in NASCAR. Sportsbooks will put a handful of drivers in groups and ask which will be the winner of the group.Top Car Make DriverThis is also specific to NASCAR, where you can bet on whether the winning driver will be in a particular car manufacturer, like Ford or Chevy. It's more applicable here since there are only two drivers on each F1 constructor, while car brands can span several NASCAR teams.Team of Race WinnerThis is similar to Outright Winner for drivers but applies to teams and constructors.Qualifying BetsBettors can wager on who will take pole position and which cars will be on pole. These are determined during qualifying racing, which typically takes place the day before the race. You can also bet on markets offering odds for who will finish in the top 5 or top 10 in qualifying, though these aren't necessarily  available for every race. The results of qualifying will often shift the race odds.Motor sports futures bettingFormula 1 bettingIn most cases, F1 futures usually apply to the next race. However, you can bet on season-long futures for F1 championship betting. The Drivers Championship is straightforward as it will be given to the driver who accumulates the most points over the season. The Constructors Championship takes into account the points for both team drivers. Only the top 10 finishers in each race score points, and those points are tallied over the season. The winning driver can be part of a constructors championship, but that's not always the case.NASCAR BettingNASCAR has different portions of the season. There are also different circuits like the Cup Series, the Xfinity Series and Truck Series. You can bet on marquee races for NASCAR in the futures market, and you can also wager on winners for these particular series.IndyCarThe major marquee futures market for IndyCar is the Indianapolis 500. Other than that race, there are season-long championship odds for the circuit.Can you parlay wagers in motor sports betting?While parlaying is generally not advised, as you don't get appropriate odds from sportsbooks that correspond to the actual chance of your bet winning, you are able to parlay outcomes in motor sports betting. While you can't pick multiple drivers to win an event in a parlay, you can pick multiple drivers to finish in the top 5 or top 10. You can also pick teams to finish in the top 5 or top 10.How to bet on motor sports live during a raceSportsbooks do offer live odds for motor sports, though this is likely a more prominent feature for NASCAR and IndyCar as opposed to F1. Driver and team odds will shift based on where they are in the grand scheme of the race. NASCAR and IndyCar allow for more leeway since there are more laps, while F1 can sometimes shift quickly towards one driver or team.Tips and strategies for how to bet on motor sportsDriver form does matter when it comes to racing, but the biggest predictor of success is usually how each team can adjust to conditions. Races can take place in all kinds of weather and team strategy can make or break the day. There are some teams that struggle to adjust, and bettors should know which teams those are before placing wagers. Historical track success often takes a back seat to current form. For example, Max Verstappen won the Canadian Grand Prix three years in a row and was a contender after starting second behind George Russell in 2025. Russell has had mixed results in Montreal historically but wound up winning the race after winning qualifying to take pole position.Longshots obviously don't usually win races, so they are better served as an inclusion in placement markets. You can usually back drivers who have had success on certain tracks or who have routinely finished just outside of a certain position market to break through eventually.Occasionally, a caution flag comes out when there's a crash on the track, which makes racing conditions hazardous for everyone. When this happens, there will be a safety car deployed, and all drivers must line up behind the safety car until the wreck is managed. There are different rules for each association and sometimes the race organizer makes a call in the moment, but usually, the race cannot end on a caution flag. If the wreck is too big to clear in a reasonable amount of time, the race will end despite the caution flag being signaled. Overtime doesn't really exist, but usually there will be at least one additional lap of racing should the fallout of the crash get removed in a timely manner and the safety car gets taken off the track.FAQCan you bet on motor sports?As long as you are of legal age in a state where sports betting is legitimate, you should be able to find a sportsbook which provides racing and motor sports odds.Who to bet on for the Indy 500?Because the Indy 500 typically takes place over Memorial Day weekend, you'll have to wait for a bit before placing wagers on who will win the signature event. Josef Newgarden won the Indy 500 in 2023 and 2024 but Alex Palou won in 2025 and is the reigning champion.Can you bet on SuperCross?SuperCross is a type of motorcycle racing. Some sportsbooks do offer SuperCross odds in certain states.Can you bet on motocross at DraftKings?DraftKings does provide SuperCross odds, which is a motocross competition, in select states. title: Jon Jones' former coach Mike Winkeljohn laments 'very disappointing' behavior amid Josh Hokit feud - CBS Sports
description: Winkeljohn, Jones' former coach and Hokit's current coach, weighs in on the drama between the UFC athletes
body:
Winkeljohn, Jones' former coach and Hokit's current coach, weighs in on the drama between the UFC athletes
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Years before guiding Josh Hokit to a UFC heavyweight title fight, renowned mixed martial arts coach Mike Winkeljohn helped mold Jon Jones into arguably the greatest MMA fighter in history. These days, Winkeljohn is disappointed in the man Jones has become.Trouble started brewing on Saturday shortly after Hokit fell short in a competitive fight with heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane at UFC 334. Jones took a sly dig at Hokit's performance, leading to an explosive back-and-forth on social media. Jones' since-deleted remark was an indirect response to comments Hokit previously made about his estranged Jackson Wink MMA training partner. It unraveled into a multi-day online saga, with Jones mocking Hokit for absorbing a record number of strikes in a heavyweight fight, while Hokit retorted with a laundry list of criminal charges and scandals.
Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!Winkeljohn barred Jones from his gym in 2021 after the two-division champion was arrested on charges of misdemeanor battery, domestic violence and felony injuring or tampering with a vehicle, ending a 12-year professional relationship. Jones subsequently labeled Winkeljohn a "miserable bastard." 
Winkeljohn, Hokit's current coach, weighed in on the discourse, feeling let down by Jones' ongoing behavior."It's very disappointing," Winkeljohn told Submission Radio. "You have to dig deep into why people do things, and I'll let people try to figure that out for themselves. I was always hopeful that Jon would get it one of these days and go to the next level."Winkeljohn defended Hokit for standing his ground. He argued that there was no alternative once Jones started publicly dragging him after Saturday's performance.
"But I'm really disappointed in that action right there because that's going to get a response from Josh, and you can see it going right now," Winkeljohn said. "Like everybody, when you're attacked, you have to attack back. If not, you'll be considered a weak person. I like what Josh does, the fact that he's willing to attack back when attacked."Hokit's future sparks a lot of curiosity. In 12 short months, he talked and punched his way from UFC debutant to heavyweight title challenger in Madison Square Garden. His athleticism, durability, and heart did a lot of heavy lifting on Saturday, but the 29-year-old former NFL player is relatively early in his development. Jones, 23 at the time, became the youngest UFC champion in 2011, a record that holds strong 15 years later. He recorded a record number of light heavyweight title defenses before moving up and capturing the heavyweight crown too. Hokit is a long, long way from building a comparable resume, but Winkeljohn has faith that Hokit can get there and is committed to replacing his estranged pupil with a new all-time great.
"Josh will be the best eventually," Winkeljohn said. "Right now, Jon Jones, I would still say, he's the best of all time. But that doesn't mean that Josh, being young in his career, can't change that. And that would be my goal as his coach: to help him out as much as I can to achieve that."

title: Yankees' David Bednar, Twins' Ryan Jeffers accept qualifying offer, six others reject $23.15 million QO - CBS Sports
description: Jake Bauers has already agreed to a four-year deal with the Red Sox; now the other five will look for better offe
body:
Jake Bauers has already agreed to a four-year deal with the Red Sox; now the other five will look for better offers than the QO
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Two players have accepted this year's one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer prior to Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET. deadline, and six others have declined the QO. David Bednar (Yankees) and Ryan Jeffers (Twins) are returning to their teams, for the 2027 season, while Randy Arozarena (Mariners),  Brandon Lowe (Pirates), Adrian Morejon (Padres), Trevor Rogers (Orioles), and Seiya Suzuki (Cubs) are all hitting the market.An eighth free agent, Jake Bauers, also received the QO. He agreed to a four-year, $58 million contract with the Red Sox this past weekend. Effectively, Bauers declined the QO. Because they paid CBT in 2026, the Red Sox will surrender their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in 2027 international bonus pool money, to sign Bauers. The Brewers, as a revenue-sharing receiver, will receive a compensation draft pick after the first round because the contract exceeds $50 million.The five unsigned free agents who rejected the QO are now tied to draft pick compensation. Their former teams will receive a draft pick if they sign elsewhere, and their new teams will be docked a draft pick and potentially international bonus pool money to sign them. The exact compensation depends on the team's revenue sharing and competitive balance tax (CBT) status.Here is draft pick compensation the former teams will receive if the seven qualified free agents change teams:
Free agentFormer teamCompensation draft pickRandy ArozarenaMarinersPick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50MBrandon LowePiratesPick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M  Adrian MorejonPadresPick after fourth roundTrevor RogersOriolesPick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M  Seiya SuzukiCubsPick after fourth roundCBT payors, like the Red Sox, will forfeit their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in 2027 international bonus pool money, to sign a qualified free agent. Teams that receive revenue sharing will surrender their third-highest 2027 draft pick. All other teams will surrender their second-highest 2027 draft pick and $500,000 in 2027 international bonus pool money.It must be noted that declining the QO does not mean the free agent can not return to his former team. The two sides could still work out a contract of any size and any length, including one worth less than QO, though that is very unlikely. Zac Gallen, Michael King, and Kyle Schwarber rejected the QO last offseason and then later re-signed with their teams. Free agents must meet certain criteria to be eligible for the QO. Players cannot have received the QO previously and they must have spent the most recent season with one team, meaning anyone traded in-season is ineligible. The Dodgers could not give Tarik Skubal, far and away the offseason's best free agent, the QO following his midseason acquisition.The QO is set at the average of the top 125 salaries in the most recent season and that is salaries only, not total compensation. For example, the Yankees paid Cody Bellinger a $20 million signing bonus and a $32.5 million salary in 2026. Only the $32.5 million counts toward the QO calculation. This QO was worth a record $23.15 million this winter.The current QO system replaced the old free-agent arbitration system in 2012 and will remain in effect this offseason. The upcoming collective bargaining agreement could change the QO system, if not eliminate it entirely. Entering the offseason, just 18 of the 157 free agents to receive the QO accepted it. That count is now at 20 of 165.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    David BednarOne of the more effective closers in baseball last season, Bednar closed down 35 of 39 save chances with a 2.47 ERA, 1.04 WHIP and 76 strikeouts in 69 ⅓ innings. Having him back on board means the Yankees don't need to find a new closer and can look instead to shore up the bridge to the ninth as needed.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Ryan JeffersThere had been talk that Jeffers wanted to stay with the Twins but that he'd decline the QO and then negotiate a long-term deal. There's still room to reach an extension, of course, but he now doesn't have any leverage from outside offers. It's a big win for the Twins, with Jeffers resuming his role as the everyday catcher and Victor Caratini serving as the primary backup. Jeffers hit .256/.353/.461 (127 OPS+) with 14 homers and 56 RBI is only 92 games last season. He's been one of the most productive offensive catchers in baseball over the course of the last four seasons, when healthy.

title: NBA MVP Rankings: Luka Dončić, Victor Wembanyama in a two-horse race; Stephen Curry's absence speaks volumes - CBS Sports
description: While Shai Gilgeous-Alexander goes for his third straight, he's behind the two other West stars
body:
While Shai Gilgeous-Alexander goes for his third straight, he's behind the two other West stars
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:12 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        We're nearly a month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and while some people say it's too early to start talking about MVP, we are not among those people. Right now, it's a clear two-horse race: Luka Doncic or Victor Wembanyama? There is a real split on this. Here's where I stand as of Tuesday, Nov. 17. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Luka Dončić, Lakers
The Luka Dončić we're watching right now isn't just the best offensive player in the world. He might be the best in history. Nobody has ever put up anything close to the numbers he is charting at the moment: 39 points per game with seven assists, seven boards, nearly two steals and a positively scorching 66.0 TS%, the latter being a number even the great Stephen Curry has only bested twice in his career. It's early, sure. Dončić isn't likely to keep making 3s at this rate for an entire season, and indeed we've seen some slippage of late (35% over his last four, if you really want to split hairs), but his volume remains, with 4.5 makes a night over that stretch. Dončić remains on track to break Curry's single-season record of 402 3-pointers, and he's done more off-ball shooting than in the past. 
Off catch: 5.9 PPG, up from 3.8 last yearOff screens: 4.2 PPG, up from 2.0 last yearThrow in more transition production and a 53% midrange conversion rate, per Cleaning The Glass, and you're seeing a more diverse scorer, which is to say this isn't just a guy who has started off hot on his step-back 3s (though this is a major factor, too, of course), but a guy piercing defenses from more spots with different shots. If Dončić could actually be any harder to guard than he has been in the past, we're seeing it this season. He's also defending. His 23 steals rank sixth league-wide. Only two players have recovered more defensive loose balls than his eight. Only one has taken more charges than his four. With Dončić as the primary defender, shooters are converting just 36.7% of their shots against a 45.1 expected FG%; that minus-8.6 is the fourth-largest discrepancy among all players who've contested at least 150 shots. Most importantly, the Lakers are 12-2 and tied with the Spurs atop the Western Conference. The Lakers rank as the league's top offense with a rating that balloons to 129.2 points per 100 possessions (which would be an NBA record by a long shot) with Dončić on, and a net rating, as illustrated below, that falls off a cliff when he sits. 
Look, if you have Wembanyama ahead of Dončić in the MVP race a month into the season, nobody is going to argue much with you. The oddsmakers slightly favor Wembanyama (+110 at FanDuel; Dončić is +140), who, as you'll see below, has what would qualify as a potentially unanimous case in most years. But this isn't most years. We got a dude averaging nearly 40 points for a No. 1 seed that nobody expected to be a No. 1 seed. Until one of those things changes, it's hard for me to go against Dončić. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Victor Wembanyama, Spurs
If you think Dončić's plus-35.5 on/off split (it's actually plus-32.2 without filtering for garbage time) is crazy, have a look at Wembanyama's number. 
Yes, you're reading that right. The Spurs, for all their supportive talent, fall by 42.6 points per 100 possessions when Wembanyama leaves the court (plus-29.2 on vs. minus-13.3 off), per Cleaning the Glass. By comparison, the best on/off split that Nikola Jokić has ever recorded is plus-24.8. Curry's best is plus-21.3. LeBron James' is plus-17.8. Go down that list and look at the most impactful on-off splits those guys have ever posted. Wembanyama is in another galaxy. 
And it's important to note that Wembanyama plays on a great team, as all these guys in the graphic have. The fact that there is still so much difference between when Wembanyama is on the court and when he isn't, even in a small sample, is honestly difficult to comprehend. San Antonio's three-guard lineup was supposed to be an experiment, but it's hard to know if Dylan Harper, De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle truly optimize one another or if Wembanyama is enough to make any lineup dominant in spite of traditional issues (like none of those three being a true shooter). Wembanyama is the best defensive player on the planet by an immeasurable amount. Even the stats don't do it justice. He's on pace for north of 350 blocks, a number only four players (Elmore Smith, Mark Eaton, Manute Bol and Hakeem Olajuwon) have eclipsed since blocks became an official stat in 1973, and still it's just as much, if not more, about the shots he deters scorers from even attempting. And why would they? Scorers are making just 33.6% of their shots when Wembanyama is the nearest defender, a 17% drop from their expected 50.4%. That also leads the league among all players who've defended at least 120 shots, and again, it fails to fully capture his defensive dominance. 
The fact that we've gotten this far without talking about Wembanyama's offense, as if it's a mere afterthought for a guy to be averaging 28.6 points and 11.6 rebounds in under 30 minutes a night. Wembanyama is figuring out his hot spots, prioritizing closer-to-the-basket positioning where he is a skyscraper among regular NBA buildings. He's taking two more paint shots per game than he did last season; 43% of his shots are coming from inside four feet, per Cleaning the Glass, up from 38% last season, and his 4.6 dunks per game (up from 2.7 last year) have him on pace to shatter Rudy Gobert's single-season record of 306. If I had to guess, Wembanyama's production is more sustainable than Dončić's. It's hard to imagine Dončić not hitting a rough patch from 3, and he's almost certainly not going to keep scoring 39 points per game. He'll be over 35 points per game when everything is said and done because that's what the Lakers need from him, but there's a burnout factor while Wembanyama is kind of cruising to these numbers, and the defensive impact is as natural as breathing. My gut says Wembanyama will be a clearer MVP favorite by Christmas. Keep an eye on...Assuming Dončić and Wembanyama each get to the mandated 65 games, everyone else is playing for third place at the moment. Which is crazy given the seasons some of the following names are having. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Alperen Sengun, Rockets
One of two players averaging at least 22 points, nine rebounds and seven assists, and the only player to be leading his team in all three categories. The Rockets are 11-4 with the No. 2 offense and Sengun is the center of it all. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jayson Tatum, Celtics
Tatum is averaging his normal 26.5 points per game. The shooting efficiency still hasn't come around, but he is an absolute quarterback on this Celtics team. He draws the doubles, and his 35.1% assist rate, per CTG, is a career high by a mile. The Celtics, for my money, are the best team in the East. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Giannis Antetokounmpo, Heat
Here come the Heat, who have won five straight games, with the last three wins coming over the Cavaliers, Pistons and Rockets. Antetokounmpo is averaging 28.3/12.5/5.2 with 1.3 blocks per game on 60% shooting. He's on fire from the midrange as the Heat are exploiting the soft spots in all the drop coverage they're facing. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Thunder
Gilgeous-Alexander has so much on his plate that it actually creates a clearer path to a third straight MVP if he can somehow lift Oklahoma City above all these injuries. He's trying. The Thunder are 9-5 and he's getting his 30.9 points per game, but his 58.7 true-shooting is down considerably, which makes sense as he has to force tougher shots now with fewer weapons around him. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Stephen Curry, Warriors
Curry's value can perhaps be felt most in his absence. The Warriors have lost three straight since he went out with a torn oblique, the last two by 59 points. The Warriors have outscored opponents by 13.5 points per 100 possessions with Curry on the floor this season and have been outscored by 8.3 points per 100 possessions without him. Along with Yaxel Lendeborg, who's being asked as a rookie to carry an impossibly heavy weight without Curry, Curry remains the only real lifeblood of a team that is still shockingly lifeless without him.
